notable.name: French
notable.note: no official status but a major lingua franca in media/education — Algeria is the world's second-largest Francophone country by speaker count

language.script: Arabic script (Arabic); Latin script (French, and Tamazight is also often written in Latin outside Morocco)

terrainDescription.zh: 絕大部分國土為撒哈拉沙漠，北部狹長的地中海沿岸與泰勒亞特拉斯山脈是主要人口聚居帶。
terrainDescription.en: The vast majority of the country is Sahara desert; a narrow Mediterranean coastal strip and the Tell Atlas mountains in the north hold most of the population.

plate.color: white front plate with black digits; yellow rear plate with black digits — a distinctive two-tone front/rear system

roadInfra.bollardStyle: No distinctively documented national style found — not a confirmed clue

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not independently documented for Algeria specifically — flagging as unconfirmed rather than guessing a style

historicalContext.zh: 阿爾及利亞語言政策歷經變化：1963年阿拉伯語成為唯一官方語言，2016年塔馬齊格特語（柏柏爾語）修憲後也取得官方地位；法語雖無官方地位，但因殖民歷史因素在媒體與教育領域仍廣泛使用。
historicalContext.en: Algeria's language policy has shifted over time: Arabic became the sole official language in 1963, and a 2016 constitutional amendment gave Tamazight (Berber) official status alongside it. French holds no official status but remains widely used in media and education due to colonial-era history.
